cargo-orange.note: The single accent. Always paired with ink-on-orange text, never white — black-on-orange is how hi-vis signage works. Dark mode lifts to oklch(0.7 0.19 48).

ink-on-orange.note: Text set on cargo orange. Hi-vis contrast; white would glare.

warm-paper.note: Light-mode canvas. Label stock, not white — takes the glare off a long shift. The email palette's #f3f1ed is a DIFFERENT, darker step (it backs the mail 'page'); this token is the email's 'paper'.

label-stock.note: Raised surfaces in light mode. Lighter than the canvas: elevation reads as closer to the light.

depot-ink.note: Body and heading text in light mode. A warm near-black, never a grey.

depot-graphite.note: Dark-mode canvas. Cool, so the cargo orange stays warm against it — depot at night.

depot-graphite-raised.note: Raised surfaces in dark mode, ~+3% lightness per elevation step.

stencil-grey.note: Section labels and secondary metadata. The demotion tool — reach for this before a bigger heading.

hairline.note: Borders and dividers — the entire depth mechanism. Dark mode swaps to oklch(1 0 0 / 9%) so edges read without turning milky.

delivered-green.note: RESERVED: delivered or collected, and nothing else. A good number is not green. Sole exception is a quantity ledger, where +/- reads as an account.

caution-amber.note: RESERVED: waiting or caution. Hue kept deliberately distinct from cargo orange.

route-blue.note: Maps, chart series, and the 'notified' state only. The one colour permitted alongside orange, because it never marks an action.

display.purpose: The largest numbers. Tabular, always. Rare.

metric.purpose: The MetricStat hero number — the dispatch-strip step. Tabular, always.

body.purpose: The working default. Prose caps at 65–75ch, though genuine prose is rare here.

label.purpose: The stencil-on-a-crate mark that heads panels and metric groups. Always Stencil Grey.

code.purpose: Tracking numbers, references, POs, timestamps, weights, quantities, money. Tabular with slashed zero.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Default duration for button and interactive state changes. Fast enough to feel mechanical rather than animated.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Active-state press feedback on buttons — a small mechanical acknowledgement, like a real key.

motion.name: focus-ring
motion.purpose: Focus-visible ring, shared by buttons and inputs so the panel behaves consistently under a keyboard.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one action on the screen that matters. Cargo orange with ink-on-orange text; there should rarely be two.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border: none; border-radius: 4.4px; background: var(--primary, oklch(0.665 0.185 47)); color: var(--primary-foreground, oklch(0.2 0.03 60)); font-family: var(--font-sans, 'Archivo Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: all 150ms; outline: none; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary, oklch(0.665 0.185 47)) 90%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring, oklch(0.665 0.185 47)) 50%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action. Neutral surface, no orange — borrowing the accent would steal the primary's meaning.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border: 1px solid var(--border, oklch(0.9 0.006 70)); border-radius: 4.4px; background: var(--background, oklch(0.986 0.004 80)); color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.22 0.012 60)); font-family: var(--font-sans, 'Archivo Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: all 150ms; outline: none; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--accent, oklch(0.955 0.006 75)); color: var(--accent-foreground, oklch(0.28 0.01 60)); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { border-color: var(--ring, oklch(0.665 0.185 47)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring, oklch(0.665 0.185 47)) 50%, transparent); } .ds-btn-outline:active { transform: scale(0.97); }

components.name: Input
components.description: Transparent over a hairline border. Focus shifts the border to cargo orange with a 3px ring — the same focus language as buttons.
components.css: .ds-input { height: 36px; width: 100%; min-width: 0; padding: 4px 12px; border: 1px solid var(--input, oklch(0.915 0.006 70)); border-radius: 4.4px; background: transparent; color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.22 0.012 60)); font-family: var(--font-sans, 'Archivo Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 14px; transition: color 150ms, box-shadow 150ms; outline: none; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.52 0.012 60)); } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: var(--ring, oklch(0.665 0.185 47)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring, oklch(0.665 0.185 47)) 50%, transparent); } .ds-input[aria-invalid="true"] { border-color: var(--destructive, oklch(0.577 0.22 27)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--destructive, oklch(0.577 0.22 27)) 20%, transparent); } .ds-input:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Card
components.description: A quiet container. Border plus tint step, never a shadow. Not the default answer to grouping — and never nested.
components.html:
Active deliveries

Border and tint carry the depth. No shadow, by doctrine.
components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; padding: 24px; border: 1px solid var(--border, oklch(0.9 0.006 70)); border-radius: 10.4px; background: var(--card, oklch(0.997 0.002 80)); color: var(--card-foreground, oklch(0.22 0.012 60)); font-family: var(--font-sans, 'Archivo Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-card-label { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.14em; color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.52 0.012 60)); } .ds-card-body { margin: 0; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.5; }

components.name: Status Stamp
components.description: SIGNATURE. A package status as a rubber ink-stamp on a waybill: rectangular (never a pill), uppercase, tracked, bordered and tinted, with a leading tick dot. The word and the tick do the work; the tint only confirms it.
components.html: Delivered In transit Waiting Draft
components.css: .ds-stamp { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 2px 6px; border: 1px solid; border-radius: 3px; font-family: var(--font-sans, 'Archivo Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.09em; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-stamp-dot { width: 4px; height: 4px; border-radius: 9999px; background: currentColor; opacity: 0.7; } .ds-stamp-done { border-color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--success, oklch(0.6 0.13 150)) 40%, transparent); background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--success, oklch(0.6 0.13 150)) 12%, transparent); color: var(--success, oklch(0.6 0.13 150)); } .ds-stamp-transit { border-color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary, oklch(0.665 0.185 47)) 40%, transparent); background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary, oklch(0.665 0.185 47)) 12%, transparent); color: var(--primary, oklch(0.665 0.185 47)); } .ds-stamp-wait { border-color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--warning, oklch(0.8 0.15 82)) 45%, transparent); background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--warning, oklch(0.8 0.15 82)) 15%, transparent); color: var(--warning-foreground, oklch(0.3 0.06 82)); } .ds-stamp-neutral { border-color: var(--border, oklch(0.9 0.006 70)); background: var(--muted, oklch(0.958 0.005 75)); color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.52 0.012 60)); }

components.name: Tracking Number
components.description: SIGNATURE. The waybill ID as a first-class monospace token — the recurring texture of the whole product, and the thing a user's eye hunts for on every screen. The copyable variant reveals its icon on hover.
components.css: .ds-tracking { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; margin: 0 -4px; padding: 2px 4px; border: none; border-radius: 2.4px; background: transparent; color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.22 0.012 60)); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms; } .ds-tracking:hover { background: var(--accent, oklch(0.955 0.006 75)); } .ds-tracking-value { font-family: var(--font-mono, 'JetBrains Mono Variable', ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: -0.01em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-feature-settings: 'zero' 1; } .ds-tracking-icon { color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.52 0.012 60)); opacity: 0; transition: opacity 150ms; } .ds-tracking:hover .ds-tracking-icon { opacity: 1; }

components.name: Metric Stat
components.description: SIGNATURE. A dispatch-strip metric: tabular hero number, demoted tracked label, optional signed delta. Three type levers, not size alone. The delta's green/red is a ledger, not a package status.
components.html:
In transit
1,284parcels
12.4%
components.css: .ds-metric { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; font-family: var(--font-sans, 'Archivo Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-metric-label { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.14em; color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.52 0.012 60)); } .ds-metric-row { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; } .ds-metric-value { font-size: 32px; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1; letter-spacing: -0.02em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.22 0.012 60)); } .ds-metric-unit { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.52 0.012 60)); } .ds-metric-delta { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 2px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--success, oklch(0.6 0.13 150)); }

components.name: Section Label
components.description: SIGNATURE. A stencil-on-a-crate label — the workhorse of hierarchy. Reach for this before reaching for a bigger heading.
components.css: .ds-section-label { font-family: var(--font-sans, 'Archivo Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.14em; color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.52 0.012 60)); }

components.name: Sidebar Navigation Item
components.description: Grouped nav on a canvas-coloured sidebar, separated by a border rather than a fill. The active item is marked with a cargo-orange bar — the one place the accent appears without being a button.
components.html: OrdersDriversInventory
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; padding: 8px; background: var(--sidebar, oklch(0.972 0.005 80)); border-right: 1px solid var(--sidebar-border, oklch(0.9 0.006 70)); font-family: var(--font-sans, 'Archivo Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-nav-item { position: relative; padding: 8px 12px; border-radius: 4.4px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; text-decoration: none; color: var(--sidebar-foreground, oklch(0.22 0.012 60)); transition: background-color 150ms; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: var(--sidebar-accent, oklch(0.95 0.006 75)); } .ds-nav-item-active::before { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); width: 3px; height: 60%; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--sidebar-primary, oklch(0.665 0.185 47)); } .ds-nav-item-active { background: var(--sidebar-accent, oklch(0.95 0.006 75)); font-weight: 600; }

narrative.overview:
Dispatch is the panel a courier depot is run from. The governing image is not a website and not a dashboard — it is a piece of operational equipment: hi-vis exactly where a hand must act, quiet and legible everywhere else, and utterly calm under load. Every surface earns its place by helping someone move a parcel from purchase order to signed proof of delivery without dropping the thread. If an element does not help someone act, confirm, or prove, it does not belong on the panel.

Light mode is warm label stock — the paper a waybill is printed on. Dark mode is cool depot-at-night graphite, which exists because the work does not stop when the light does, and because a single cargo orange reads like a hi-vis vest against it. Depth is carried by borders and small tonal shifts between surfaces, never by shadow: this is a tool, and tools are flat. Density is high because the users are experts who are in this all day, but density is paid for with hierarchy — size, weight, and colour working together so a one-second glance finds the one thing that matters.

The system explicitly rejects the registers it could easily have drifted into. Not a generic SaaS dashboard: no gradients, no identical rounded card grids, no hero-metric theatre. Not enterprise logistics software: no undifferentiated grey wall where everything has the same weight. Not a consumer parcel-tracking app: nothing playful, animated, or celebratory in a tool that someone operates for eight hours.
keyCharacteristics: One accent (cargo orange), reserved for action and brand — roughly 10% of any screen.
Colour is semantic before it is decorative; green means delivered, and nothing else.
Flat by doctrine: borders and surface tint, never shadow.
Machine values (references, codes, timestamps, weights, money) are always monospace and tabular.
Hierarchy from size plus weight plus colour — never size alone.
Legible at a glance on a phone, under depot glare, held one-handed.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Cargo orange is the only accent, and it appears on no more than ~10% of any screen. Its rarity is what makes it mean "act here". A screen where two things are orange is a screen where nothing is.

rules.name: The Reserved Colour Rule
rules.body: Signal colours are vocabulary, not decoration, and each has exactly one meaning: Delivered Green = delivered or collected, and nothing else, ever. Caution Amber = waiting or caution, kept deliberately distinct in hue from cargo orange. Returned Red = returned or destructive. If you want green because a number is good, you want the wrong colour — the one documented exception is a ledger of quantities (inventory movements, delivered value), where +/- green/red reads as an account rather than a package status.

rules.name: The Orange-Is-Not-Ink Rule
rules.body: Cargo orange measures 3.3:1 on a light surface — it is a surface colour and a marker, never body text. text-primary below 18px (or below 14px bold) fails WCAG AA on the light theme, tinted backgrounds included; the orange looks fine to a designer on a bright monitor and disappears under depot glare. Set the text in ink and let the orange carry the tint, the border, the underline, or the fill behind ink-on-orange. Dark mode passes comfortably (6.4:1), so this is a light-theme rule — and light is where the depot works by day. Measure, don't eyeball.

rules.name: The Never-Colour-Alone Rule
rules.body: No state is communicated by hue alone. Depot glare, a one-second glance, and colour blindness all break it. Every status carries a word, a mark, or a shape as well — which is why a package status is a stamp with text and a tick, not a coloured dot.

rules.name: The Three Levers Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from size, weight, and colour together. Making a thing bigger is the laziest of the three and the first to break a dense screen; a demoted label at the same size in Stencil Grey does more work than a point size ever will.

rules.name: The Machine Value Rule
rules.body: If a value came from a machine and a human might read it aloud, type it, or compare it in a column, it is monospace and tabular. Tracking numbers, references, POs, timestamps, weights, quantities, money. No exceptions — a tracking number set in the body face is a bug.

rules.name: The Flat Tool Rule
rules.body: No decorative shadows, no glassmorphism, no blur. Shadows imply objects floating in space; this is a panel, and a panel's parts are set into the surface. If a surface needs to separate, give it a border or a tint step. If it needs to lift, ask whether it should be a dialog instead.

rules.name: The Audit Test
rules.body: If a screenshot looks like it could carry a drop shadow without anything changing, the borders are doing too little work. Fix the border and the tint step, not the shadow.

dos: Do bind to semantic tokens (bg-primary, text-muted-foreground, border-border). Raw hex or a Tailwind grey is always a bug — it breaks dark mode silently.
Do set every machine-produced value in .mono with tabular figures: tracking numbers, references, POs, timestamps, weights, quantities, money.
Do build depth from borders and a tint step of ~3% lightness per elevation level.
Do reach for the dispatch signatures (StatusStamp, TrackingNumber, RouteTimeline, MetricStat, SectionLabel) before inventing a new pattern, and for shadcn primitives before raw HTML.
Do demote with Stencil Grey and the 11px tracked label before promoting with size.
Do give every status a word or a mark alongside its colour.
Do keep cargo orange to ~10% of the screen, and to actions and brand only.
Do use the searchable Combobox for any data-backed dropdown.
Do design for the worst case: a phone under depot glare, one-handed, glanced at for a second.
Do give every animation a prefers-reduced-motion alternative.
donts: Don't ship anything that reads as a generic SaaS dashboard — no gradients, no gradient text, no identical rounded card grids, no hero-metric theatre, no decorative illustration.
Don't ship anything that reads as enterprise logistics software — a grey wall where every element has the same weight is the failure mode this design exists to avoid.
Don't ship anything that reads as a consumer parcel-tracking app — nothing playful, celebratory, or animated for its own sake in a tool someone operates all day.
Don't use green for anything but delivered or collected. A good number is not green. The only exception is a quantity ledger, where +/- reads as an account.
Don't put cargo orange on a secondary action, a status, or a decoration. If two things are orange, neither is primary.
Don't set small text in text-primary on a light surface — it measures 3.3:1 and fails AA. See the Orange-Is-Not-Ink Rule.
Don't add a drop shadow, a glass blur, or a backdrop-filter. This is a tool; tools are flat.
Don't use a coloured border-left as an accent stripe on cards, rows, or callouts. Use a full border, a tint, or a stamp.
Don't nest a card inside a card.
Don't communicate state with a bare coloured dot.
Don't build hierarchy from size alone.
Don't use a pill radius on a status — the stamp is rectangular, and that is the point.
Don't let a workflow push someone back to a spreadsheet, a phone call, or paper. That is a design failure, not a user habit.
